highlight.text: My pictures seem to be quite simple and carelessly done, but true connoisseurs will realize that they are very close to the old models and may therefore be considered good.
highlight.lead: Zhao Mengfu, in a colophon of 1299:

source.author: Zhao Mengfu (Chao Meng-fu)
source.title: Colophon, 1299
source.publisher: translated in Osvald Sirén, A History of Early Chinese Painting, vol. II (The Medici Society, 1933; Internet Archive scan)

work.text: It was not through originality of invention or new ideas that Chao Meng-fu acquired his great fame as a painter, but rather through his faithful insistence on classical traditions and great technical proficiency.

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: A History of Early Chinese Painting, vol. II

moment.text: Among the four great painters of the Yiian dynasty Chao Meng-fu ranked first, then came Huang Kung-wang, Wang Meng, and Wu Chen.

matters.text: In the suave and competent Chao Meng-fu the conquerors found an ideal link between their own crude barbarism and the age-long civilization of their victims.
